gaps.title: Self-contained release binaries: static musl (or a pinned glibc floor), aarch64, size budget and a minimal image
gaps.strength: C-level speed in tiny, self-contained binaries built for an explicit target (x86_64 and aarch64), shipped in a scratch image
sources: `blockblaz/zeam`: [.github/workflows/auto-release.yml](https://github.com/blockblaz/zeam/blob/HEAD/.github/workflows/auto-release.yml) (`zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu` and `-Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu`, one release per arch)
`blockblaz/zeam`: [Dockerfile.prebuilt](https://github.com/blockblaz/zeam/blob/HEAD/Dockerfile.prebuilt) (`FROM scratch` runtime with only the libraries `ldd` lists)
`stateless-consensus/phant`: [build.zig](https://github.com/stateless-consensus/phant/blob/HEAD/build.zig) (`standardTargetOptions`: any target triple, static libraries for its C dependencies)
`paradigmxyz/reth`: [Cargo.toml](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/36600d5ff9628465475dd4c7608e2e9f2fe24273/Cargo.toml) (release profiles; reth publishes x86_64 and aarch64 binaries)
gaps.ours: `ci/release.sh` builds `target/release/xone` for the host only (linux-x86_64); `Dockerfile` says "it links glibc dynamically" on an `ubuntu:24.04` base; `docs/ops/release.md` "Not covered here": aarch64. Measured on the current build: `objdump -T target/release/xone` needs `GLIBC_2.38`; `ldd` lists libc, libm, libgcc_s; size 19.4 MB, not stripped; `Cargo.toml` has no `[profile.release]`
gaps.priority_reason: P1 (impact on operators): the release binary needs GLIBC_2.38, so it does not start on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35) or Debian 12 (2.36), which many XDC masternode hosts run. The Docker image hides this, a tarball install does not.

gaps.title: Compressed frozen segments: zstd for closed XSEG chunks of headers, bodies and receipts (and changesets once #135 moves them)
gaps.strength: smallest archive: immutable history in compressed segment files (Erigon `.seg` with a pattern dictionary; reth NippyJar with zstd dictionaries)
sources: `erigontech/erigon`: [db/seg/decompress.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/bbb5524e53fb057e7d47a5066e152f1091ac4ba4/db/seg/decompress.go) (random access by offset into a compressed segment)

`erigontech/erigon`: [docs/site/docs/get-started/hardware-requirements.mdx](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/bbb5524e53fb057e7d47a5066e152f1091ac4ba4/docs/site/docs/get-started/hardware-requirements.mdx) (an Ethereum archive node fits on one 4 TB drive)
gaps.ours: `docs/adr/ADR-005-storage-and-publication.md` section 6.1: a frame is `payload_len | block | payload | crc32c` with raw RLP; `BLOCKS_PER_FILE = 100_000`; `crates/xone-db/src/segments.rs` has no compression; only the snapshot export (`crates/xone-sync/src/bootstrap/format.rs`) uses gzip. #149: xone-rs Apothem datadir 72 GB against 13 GB for xOneGo
gaps.priority_reason: P2 (impact on operators): disk is the main cost of an XDC node and the xone-rs Apothem datadir is the largest of the xOne family (72 GB, #149). History grows with chain length; compression is the largest saving that does not change any format a peer or a consensus rule sees.

gaps.title: Seeded history distribution: nodes serve their committed XSEG chunks with a hash manifest, new nodes fetch from several seeds and verify
gaps.strength: seeded distribution of immutable history: every node seeds its finished snapshot files and a new node downloads them from many peers by content hash
sources: `erigontech/erigon`: [cmd/downloader/readme.md](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/bbb5524e53fb057e7d47a5066e152f1091ac4ba4/cmd/downloader/readme.md) ("Service to seed/download historical data (snapshots, immutable .seg files)"; new snapshots start seeding automatically)

`erigontech/erigon`: [db/downloader/chaintoml.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/bbb5524e53fb057e7d47a5066e152f1091ac4ba4/db/downloader/chaintoml.go) (published list of snapshot hashes per chain)
gaps.ours: `bin/xone/src/cmd/snapshot.rs` exports and imports one archive with pins (#38, closed); GAP-0034 (#185) adds import from one HTTPS URL. Plan #1 (B3.7) and #38 say: hash-named segment files with a manifest over HTTPS; "no torrent; add it only if public demand appears". No node serves its chunks
gaps.priority_reason: P3 (impact on operators): a new XDC node can already snap-sync state and import a pinned snapshot (#38); this removes the single-server dependency for history and spreads the load, but no operator is blocked without it.

gaps.title: History backfill after snap sync: download headers, bodies and receipts below the pivot in the background, to a configurable barrier
gaps.strength: fast sync: state at a pivot plus FastBlocks, which downloads headers, bodies and receipts below the pivot in parallel, back to configurable barriers
gaps.ours: `spec/snap/completeness.md` and `spec/retention.md`: a snap node fetches only the ranges the first block after the pivot needs (rows 3, 7, 11; "none below the pivot" for reorg); `crates/xone-snap/src/client.rs` `Need { kind, first, last }`; `docs/ops/net2040-sync-modes.md`: snap datadir 72 MB. No background download below the pivot
gaps.priority_reason: P2 (impact on operators): a snap-synced xone-rs node holds almost nothing below its pivot, so it cannot answer eth_getLogs, receipts or old blocks, and it serves GetBlockBodies poorly to peers (#125). An operator who wants a full-history RPC node today must full-sync from genesis.

gaps.title: RPC traffic recorder and open-loop replay benchmark (record real requests, replay them at a set rate, report latency per method)

sources: `NethermindEth/nethermind`: [tools/Kute/README.md](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a7dd73052e696ad934d228aad3f33e660701fdb7/tools/Kute/README.md) (replays recorded JSON-RPC messages, measures the node)
gaps.ours: `docs/perf.md` section 4 requires open-loop load (latency from the intended send time) and `bench/workloads/*.yaml` specify workloads, but `bench/` has only `collect/env.sh` and `summarise.py`: no load generator and no recorder. `conformance/rpc-parity` checks values, not load

priority_rule_advantages: Second pass (strengths): priority by impact for an XDC node operator, not by competitor count. P1 = operators are blocked or forced into a workaround today; P2 = large cost or capability gain for many operators; P3 = integrators, private networks or maintainers.
priority_rule_pass3: Third pass: operator impact first (P1 = operators blocked or forced into a workaround today; P2 = large cost or capability gain for many operators; P3 = integrators, private networks or maintainers), raised one level (never above P1) when 8+ of the 14 selected competitors have it, or when a canonical XDC client (XDPoSChain, the geth-XDC oracle pin) ships it in a namespace or default the fleet uses.
